wortfallen.lead: Some words look or sound almost the same – and mean something completely different. Here are the {n} funniest traps, each with a memory trick.
wortfallen.kitchen.m2: a farm bird; also its meat
wortfallen.kitchen.react: A whole kitchen? With the fridge and the sink? You must be really hungry!
wortfallen.kitchen.tip: One sentence for both: the chicken is in the kitchen. You can eat only one of them.
wortfallen.sheep.m2: a farm animal with wool (long ee)
wortfallen.sheep.react: On a sheep? That was a slow and very woolly trip!
wortfallen.sheep.tip: ship: short i, quick like a wave. sheep: long ee – make it as long as the sheep's baaa.
wortfallen.hungry.react: Angry? With me? What have I done?
wortfallen.hungry.tip: hungry starts with h, like hamburger. angry starts with a, like argh!
wortfallen.walk.react: You do your job on the way there? That's very busy!
wortfallen.walk.tip: In walk the l is silent and the sound is long, like in door: /wɔːk/. work sounds like bird: /wɜːk/.
wortfallen.become.m2: to change into something, to start to be
wortfallen.become.react: You want to turn into a coffee? Hot and black?
wortfallen.become.tip: False friend for German speakers: bekommen = get. become = werden: She became a doctor.
wortfallen.gift.m2: it makes you ill or kills you
wortfallen.gift.react: A present in a bottle? How lovely! Can I open it?
wortfallen.gift.tip: False friend for German speakers: Gift = poison. In English a gift is always a present.
wortfallen.actual.react: And the other prices? Were they not real?
wortfallen.actual.tip: False friend: aktuell (German), actuel (French), attuale (Italian), actual (Spanish) = current. In English, actual means real: the actual price is the price you really pay.
wortfallen.eventually.m2: in the end, after a long time
wortfallen.eventually.react: So you'll definitely come – just very, very late?
wortfallen.eventually.tip: False friend: eventuell (German), éventuellement (French), eventualmente (Spanish, Italian) = maybe. eventually = in the end.
wortfallen.sensible.react: Sensible? Then he'll understand why you're shouting!
wortfallen.sensible.tip: False friend: sensibel (German), sensible (French, Spanish) = sensitive. In English, sensible means practical: sensible shoes for a long walk.
wortfallen.embarrassed.m1: you feel silly in front of other people
wortfallen.embarrassed.m2: a baby is growing inside you
wortfallen.embarrassed.react: Embarrassed? But a baby is wonderful news!
wortfallen.embarrassed.tip: False friend for Spanish speakers: embarazada = pregnant. embarrassed = you go red because you feel silly.
wortfallen.library.m1: you borrow books there, for free
wortfallen.library.react: You paid at the library? There you borrow books – for free!
wortfallen.library.tip: False friend: librería (Spanish), librairie (French), libreria (Italian) = bookshop. A library lends books.
wortfallen.chef.react: Your chef? I didn't know you worked in a restaurant!
wortfallen.chef.tip: False friend: Chef (German), chef (French) = boss. In English, a chef cooks in a restaurant kitchen.
wortfallen.handy.m1: a phone you carry with you
wortfallen.handy.react: Your handy what? Your handy umbrella?
wortfallen.handy.tip: False friend for German speakers: das Handy = mobile (UK) or cell phone (US). In English, handy is an adjective: useful.
wortfallen.borrow.m1: to take something and give it back later
wortfallen.borrow.m2: to give something and get it back later
wortfallen.borrow.react: Borrow you? From whom? You're not a library book!
wortfallen.borrow.tip: You borrow FROM someone; someone lends TO you. The bank lends you money – you borrow money from the bank.
wortfallen.fun.react: Funny? Did somebody tell jokes all night?
wortfallen.fun.tip: fun = you enjoy it. funny = it makes you laugh. A holiday is fun; a clown is funny.
wortfallen.factory.m1: a building where things are made
wortfallen.factory.react: A car made of fabric? Soft, but not very safe!
wortfallen.factory.tip: False friend: Fabrik (German), fábrica (Spanish), fabbrica (Italian) = factory. fabric = cloth, material.
wortfallen.receipt.m1: the paper you get when you pay
wortfallen.receipt.m2: it tells you how to cook something
wortfallen.receipt.react: The recipe? Do you want to cook the shoes?
wortfallen.receipt.tip: receipt: the p is silent (/rɪˈsiːt/), you get it at the till. recipe has three syllables (/ˈresəpi/) and lives in the kitchen.

kt.t.title: Placement test for your class
kt.t.lead: Your class takes the test on their phones via a QR code, with their names and without an account. You see each person's level, from A1 to B2, and which topics they haven't got yet. Or run a topic test to check the grammar of one level. The questions come from our grammar exercises; you can edit any of them.
kt.t.signin.title: Sign in to create a test
kt.t.signin.text: The results belong to your account, so you can still see them next week. The account is free. Your students don't need one.
kt.t.teacher.text: Then turn on the teacher tools: class tests, surveys, classes and your own live quizzes. You can turn them off again at any time under Settings in your account.

kt.t.umfang.langInfo: About an hour for A1 to B2, less with fewer levels. One reading text and one listening text per level, plus a writing task that you mark. Everyone needs headphones for the listening.
kt.t.preview.hint: This is what the test looks like, with the correct answer first. You can edit any question and its answers or write your own; they stay when you reshuffle. Each phone shows the answers in a different order.
kt.t.how.title: How the test works
kt.t.how.1: The class scans the QR code, enters their names and answers one question after another. They can skip questions.
kt.t.how.2: Each phone can submit once. Afterwards each person sees their own score and which questions were wrong, but not the answers. You go through those with the class.
kt.t.how.3: We save the name, the answers and the score. No account, no email, no IP address. You can delete single results or the whole test.
